summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of bioprosthetic aortic valve, pacemaker, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, chronic diastolic heart failure, and recurrent cellulitis was admitted for rapidly progressive right leg erythema and pain, consistent with cellulitis, despite being on suppressive cephalexin. She presented with fever and developed septic shock requiring vasopressors and ICU care. Blood cultures grew Morganella, and imaging ruled out necrotizing infection and DVT. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, transitioned to vancomycin and meropenem, and discharged on a two-week course of IV ertapenem via PICC line. Due to a subtherapeutic INR of 1.8 and recent TIA history, she was bridged with Lovenox. Her renal dysfunction resolved, and she improved clinically, returning to baseline home medications. She was discharged home with home health support for IV antibiotics and follow-up arranged.
